acceptance_thresholds_frozen_now.notes: a slice that has not reached 200 closed trades cannot accept or reject anything, and is reported as ACCRUING rather than as a verdict

comparator_CURRENT: the runtime as it stands: no strategy admitted, no trades, flat equity. A candidate must beat that flat line net of the declared costs, not merely exist

costs.why: the same declared parity inputs the engine comparison used, so the holdout is scored under the same model rather than a kinder one; spread and slippage are held at zero here because they are model inputs and the paper broker's 1 bps per side is reported separately

entry_and_exit_rules.entry: long while ema(12) > ema(26) on the previous closed 1h bar; fill at the open of the next bar
entry_and_exit_rules.exit: flat when ema(12) < ema(26) on a closed bar; fill at the open of the next bar
entry_and_exit_rules.open_position_at_window_end: force-closed at the final bar's open on both engines

hypothesis: H0: this rule's net expectancy per trade is <= 0 after the declared costs. H1: it is > 0. The measurement window is exhausted at 2026-10-16T15:00:00Z, so every bar at or after that instant is prospective with respect to it

instruments_and_timeframes.venue: binance (public OHLCV through ccxt, read-only, no credentials)

strategies_and_parameters.parameter_source: frozen before capture; no fitting, no search, no walk-forward

why_a_new_slice_is_needed: the frozen corpus has been read by candidate experiments and by the engine comparison, so any further scoring on it is in-sample. Mechanical parity between engines can and has been tested on historical bars; economic inference requires a slice that no decision has touched
